lede: The most consequential meeting this week is Mountain Village Town Council on Thursday, August 20, where a resolution setting the sale price appreciation cap for deed-restricted affordable units is up for a vote — the fine print that determines whether workforce housing actually stays affordable long-term. The same evening, Telluride's Planning and Zoning Commission holds a public hearing and takes a first formal look at the school district's employee housing proposal for the middle-high school site on W. Colorado. Meanwhile, the Town of Telluride's brand-new Resident Advisory Committee holds its inaugural meeting, giving employee-housing tenants a structured voice on rental policies for the first time.

notable.stake: Vote sets appreciation cap controlling whether affordable units stay affordable.
Public hearing plus first review of school district employee housing construction proposal.
Inaugural tenant advisory body; residents elect leadership and shape rental policy role.
